description: We are Team KnevaX, a passionate group of AI enthusiasts, developers, and problem-solvers participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project, Flame in Freefall, focuses on using AI and data analysis to explore microgravity combustion and improve fire safety insights for space missions. We aim to combine machine learning, data visualization, and innovative thinking to develop a meaningful, science-driven solution.
summary: FlameWise is an interactive dashboard, powered by SI, that turns decades of NASA microgravity combustion research into fire-safety insights for crews heading to the Moon and Mars. It brings together 10 NASA investigations (BASS-II, Saffire I–III, SAME, SAME-R, FLEX, ACME/BRE, DAFT), 136 test records and 20 sources into one evidence trail. It answers the challenge's three asks. It summarizes the evidence with AI answers where every paragraph must cite a real NASA source. It ranks insights by how much checkable evidence supports them. It interprets each finding by saying what it means for a crew and where it stops applying. A live 3D flame shows how fire changes as gravity disappears, and a gap matrix shows that the collection holds no direct lunar or Martian fire data. This matters because a confident wrong answer about fire in a habitat is dangerous: FlameWise gives fast answers without letting them become false conclusions.
details:
FlameWise – NASA Microgravity Fire Research Dashboard

Live Website: https://flame-wise.vercel.app/
GitHub Repository: https://github.com/Hameed-Ur-Rehman25/FlameWise

1. What It Does

FlameWise is an interactive web dashboard designed to explore and analyze NASA's microgravity fire research. It brings research findings, experimental data, and scientific evidence together in one platform through nine integrated views:

  • Briefing: Interactive 3D flame visualization and gravity dial.
  • Dashboard: Research measurements, datasets, and coverage overview.
  • Insights: Six ranked research findings and a Moon/Mars evidence-gap matrix.
  • Mission Scenario: Matches habitat materials, oxygen levels, and airflow conditions with relevant studies, highlighting limitations in applying existing research.
  • Evidence Archive: Searchable research archive with AI-generated summaries.
  • Compare: Side-by-side comparison of NASA investigations.
  • Data Lab: Interactive charts with CSV and JSON export.
  • Ask the Evidence: AI-powered question answering with source citations.
  • Sources & Method: Research references, methodology, and evidence evaluation criteria.

2. How the Intelligence Works

FlameWise uses an evidence-based retrieval and AI synthesis pipeline.

When a user submits a question, the system identifies relevant NASA investigations, source passages, and experimental records. Google's Gemini model then generates an answer using only the retrieved evidence.

To maintain reliability, the server validates every answer. It rejects uncited paragraphs and citations to sources that were not provided to the AI. If validation fails, the system displays a clearly labeled alternative answer generated directly from retrieved evidence.

Research insights are ranked using a transparent evidence-strength score based on:

  • Verified experimental records.
  • Page-located research passages.
  • Quantitative findings, weighted twice.

Importantly, findings are ranked by evidence strength, not by perceived danger.

3. Benefits and Impact

FlameWise helps mission planners, researchers, and students quickly discover relevant scientific evidence, understand the reliability of research findings, and identify gaps in existing knowledge.

Its evidence-gap matrix highlights an important limitation: the collection contains microgravity research but no direct lunar or Martian fire-test data.

This distinction helps identify the additional research required before applying existing findings to future lunar and Martian habitats.

4. Trust and Scientific Reliability

Scientific accuracy and responsible interpretation are central to FlameWise.

The platform deliberately avoids:

  • Declaring materials universally safe.
  • Predicting fire probabilities without sufficient evidence.
  • Recommending unsupported fire-suppressant dosages.

It also preserves scientific data integrity:

  • Missing measurements remain empty rather than being converted to zero.
  • Unusual sensor readings remain visible and are flagged.
  • Every reported measurement can be traced to its NASA source and corresponding PDF page.

5. Technology Stack

Component

The application has no frontend runtime dependencies and can also operate offline as a standalone HTML file.

6. Creative Approach

One distinctive design decision is the visualization of partial-gravity conditions.

The 3D flame visualization represents partial gravity using grey, hatched styling because the available research collection contains no supporting data for those conditions.

Rather than presenting unsupported scientific conclusions, the visualization makes the absence of evidence visible to users.

7. Use of AI Tools

The development team used SI coding assistants to support code development and text drafting. All generated material was reviewed by the team.

Gemini powers the application's in-platform question-answering functionality. These responses are explicitly labeled "AI Synthesis" to distinguish AI-generated interpretations from original scientific records.
